evals.prompt: red-team session-cache-design.md properly before I take it to arch review. I want severities on every finding and a way to re-check them after I fix things. This backs our checkout flow, so wrong prices or a Redis meltdown are the nightmares.
evals.expected_output: A severity-graded red-team report: a charter naming ranked harm categories, findings from multiple lenses each with a concrete reproducible failure scenario, root cause, suggested fix, Confirmed/Plausible status, plus a retest list. Should catch high-impact flaws such as the KEYS-based invalidation blocking the shared Redis cluster, stale-price windows, and sizing math (200k x 40KB = 8GB, exactly the free space).
expectations: Every finding carries a severity grade and all findings appear in one strict total rank order (no flat band of same-grade ties without sub-ranking)
Every finding includes a concrete failure scenario naming specific inputs, state, or sequence leading to a specific outcome

Report flags the KEYS-based invalidation blocking the shared Redis cluster AND ranks this guaranteed recurring failure at or above any conditional finding that depends on an unverified fact (such as the eviction-policy-dependent sizing collision)
Report flags the sizing math: 200k sessions x 40KB = 8GB, equal to all free memory on the shared cluster
Report flags a wrong/stale price window (TTL or invalidation gap can quote users outdated prices or tax)
Retest mechanism is one falsifiable per-finding check (yes/no verifiable against a revised design), not a verbatim copy of the full failure scenarios
Review states an explicit charter/threat model with ranked harm categories before the findings
Report opens or closes with a bottom-line verdict plus a minimum-changes path that collapses the findings into fewer fixes than findings
Coverage extends beyond the three planted flaws: report raises at least one of staleness/invalidation observability, cache keyspace namespacing, or rollout gating between 5% and 100%

evals.prompt: attack this on-call rotation plan and grade the findings by severity - what would actually break and how bad? oncall-rotation-plan.md
evals.expected_output: A severity-graded adversarial review with an explicit threat model, findings anchored to downstream harm (e.g. coverage gaps outside the two 12-hour windows given timezones, a 6-week-old team with no prod experience or access owning Sev1s, US-only IC pool defeating the zero-overnight-pages goal, vague runbook handover), each with failure scenario, root cause, fix, and a retest list.
expectations: Every finding carries a severity grade and all findings appear in one strict total rank order
Every finding includes a concrete failure scenario tied to downstream harm
Report identifies the timezone coverage gap: Krakow 08:00-20:00 CET = 02:00-14:00 ET, leaving 20:00-02:00 ET covered by neither window
Report identifies Krakow readiness risk: 6-week-old team, no production experience, access provisioning incomplete before go-live
Report identifies that the US-only incident-commander pool still wakes US engineers, undermining the zero-overnight-pages metric
Report states plainly (in a verdict or top-ranked finding) that the plan fails its own stated goal as written, not merely a list of individual risks
Coverage includes at least two of: cross-shift handover of in-flight incidents, weekend or US/Polish holiday misalignment, DST drift between US and EU changeover weeks, rollback/abort criteria
Retest mechanism is one falsifiable per-finding check, not verbatim scenario copies
Report includes a bottom-line verdict plus a prioritized minimum-changes list
